newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Profit taking clouds Belgian OLO market's picture.
newsitem.headline: Profit taking clouds Belgian OLO market's picture.

text.p: Profit taking has for now clouded the big picture for the Belgian OLO market, analysts said on Thursday, but traders said the short-term trend remained firm.

Kredietbank market economist Conrad Fieremans said the benchmark 10-year OLO yield could hit 5.90 percent by the end of the year but Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet's Francoise Bernard did not think this was likely until the first quarter of 1997.
Traders noted that Wednesday's profit taking, that pushed the benchmark 10-year yield to 5.77 from 5.72 percent, stopped Thursday morning on news of a rise in Germany's jobless rate.
The 2006 OLO was back down to 5.76 percent by mid-morning.
The 10-year OLO/Bund spread was steady at 11 basis points.

"I cannot see any lower levels in the coming days," Fieremans said. "The danger for me is still the U.S.. The economy is clearly rebounding, but so far this does not seem to have been noticed. At some point market sentiment will change."

Bernard agreed long-term rates could push up toward the end of the year, especially if there was renewed profit taking. But she expected the Bundesbank to seek to keep pressure off short term rates by lowering its minimum reserve requirement on repos.
"Germany has to meet the Maastricht criteria. Higher rates means a higher deficit," she said.

Bernard said she was not worried at all by the U.S. economy. Only if the Dow significantly broke 6,500 points might the Fed be tempted to raise rates. Fieremans also said he did not expect the Fed to raise rates at the next December 17 FOMC meeting.

Meanwhile, traders said the market remained firm, despite Wednesday's drop. One noted that the Belgian central bank's issue of around 100 billion francs of certificates of deposits in the last two weeks had not hit either short or long-term rates, and the spread over Bunds remained undented.
"It just shows how much cash there is in the institutions," he said.
"I would not be surprised to see the spread over Bunds fall below 10 basis points again (in the coming days)," he said.
He added however that business would likely be subdued ahead of the publication of Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls report.
